1.0.0.en: An apostle ... by the will of God: St. Paul was in the distress of prison, awaiting death, yet he trusts that God called him to this ministry and to endure sufferings, so he is not troubled by afflictions and death. The promise of life: in his affliction he looks to the glories of eternal life that Christ promised him, so he is able to endure the affliction and even to make light of it.

1.0.1.en: The Apostle declares his confidence in God's choosing him to preach in His name, so he is not troubled by the distress of prison or by the death that awaits him, because he is awaiting the Kingdom of Heaven.

1.1.0.en: My dearly beloved son: Timothy was the closest of his disciples to his heart, and at the end of Paul's life he sends him his last epistle and shows his feelings toward him, calling him beloved.

1.1.1.en: Grace, mercy and peace: he asks for him and for the Church of Ephesus, which faces afflictions, grace from God to help them, mercy to cover them, and peace within their hearts despite the outward afflictions.

1.1.2.en: St. Paul sends this epistle to his disciple Timothy, who was close and very dear to his heart, and asks for him and for the Church of Ephesus, of which he is bishop, comforts and help from God.

1.1.3.en: Look to the reward of blessed eternity so that you may be able to endure the sufferings you are passing through, and at the same time the delights of the world will become small in your eyes, and you will reject sin, however small, lest it hinder you from your goal.

1.2.s.en: (2) His love and encouragement of him

1.2.0.en: Whom I serve from my forefathers: Paul thanks God, who made Himself known to him through his Jewish forefathers, so he enjoyed the knowledge of Him, unlike the Gentiles who went astray in their thinking, did not know God and worshiped idols. With a pure conscience: St. Paul held fast to God with purity of heart, even when he was persecuting the Christians, for he thought this was serving God, until Christ met him on the road to Damascus and corrected his course. That without ceasing I have remembrance of thee: Paul trained himself in prayer by night and day, and his love for Timothy appeared in his concern to pray for him in all his prayers.

1.2.1.en: St. Paul is careful to pray, giving thanks to the God to whom he had been bound since his childhood, and he also prays for others, especially his beloved son Timothy, for he had grown accustomed to constant prayer.

1.3.0.en: Paul's fatherhood and his tender feelings appear, and also Timothy's sonship, evident in his tears, whether when he bade Paul farewell, or when Paul was in his first imprisonment in Rome, and on various other occasions. The father and his son are marked by deep feelings of love, and therefore he longs to see him, to be satisfied with seeing him and to rejoice in meeting him.

1.4.0.en: The Apostle praises Timothy's faith and describes it as pure and without ulterior motive. He received it from his mother and grandmother, who were distinguished by the strength of their faith, for they were devout Jewish women. Timothy learned this faith in simplicity, not through words alone, but through the conduct of his mother and grandmother, and therefore this faith was firmly established in him, for Paul tells him that it dwelt in him. By this praise he encourages him in his affliction and calls him not to be troubled before the affliction, and he gives the credit to his mother and grandmother so that he may not become proud.

1.5.1.en: The gift of God: the blessings of the sacrament of the priesthood.

1.5.2.en: By the putting on of my hands: the rite of the sacrament of the priesthood was performed by the bishop's laying his hands on the head of the one presented for ordination, with prayers.

1.5.3.en: Concerning Timothy's relationship with Paul, he reminds him of the grace of the sacrament of the priesthood which he received at his hands, and asks him to kindle the Holy Spirit who is in him by faithfulness in his ministry.

1.6.0.en: The spirit of fear: the despair and discouragement that Timothy could fall into because of the many afflictions and responsibilities that face him, especially since he is young.

1.6.1.en: The spirit of power: God's power, which supports in afflictions.

1.6.2.en: Love: which appears in his care and concern for his people, for together with strong faith there is tender love that joins him with his people in one unity in God.

1.6.3.en: Counsel: guiding his children so that they do not fall into heresies and remain firm in the faith and the spiritual life. After Paul spoke of Timothy's relationship with his family through the faith he received from them, and then his relationship with the Apostle through the grace of the sacrament of the priesthood, he reminds him of the work of the Holy Spirit, who gives him power, the care of love, and guidance for his people despite the surrounding afflictions.

1.6.4.en: May you appreciate the feelings of others and encourage them with words of praise and pray for them, so that you support them within the afflictions of life and even gladden their hearts with your love for them, and you too are comforted by their love for you.

1.7.0.en: The testimony of our Lord: preaching Christ.

1.7.1.en: The crucified Christ appeared shameful, and so did Paul in prison, so he asks his disciple Timothy to be strong in his preaching and not to be ashamed of Christ, who was dishonored for his sake, or of his father Paul, who suffers in chains, but to endure also the sufferings he meets in Ephesus during his ministry of spreading the Gospel, relying on the power of the Holy Spirit who supports him.

1.8.0.en: Paul makes clear that the salvation we enjoy is not the result of our works in themselves, but of the grace of God, who purposed our redemption before the foundation of the world and accomplished it in the fullness of time. As for the endurance of sufferings and the spiritual striving which he asks of him, it is the result of the salvation we receive and is by the support of grace, to prove the sincerity of our faith and our love for God.

1.9.0.en: Is now made manifest: he means the grace of God.

1.9.1.en: The grace of God appeared in the fullness of time by the Cross of Christ, who abolished the power of death by His death and gave us new life in Him, indeed immortality with Him forever in the Kingdom. We receive all these graces if we believe in Christ.

1.10.0.en: The grace of God chose Paul, who had been resisting Christianity, that he might believe and preach to the Gentiles who were far from God and become an apostle to them, drawing them to faith in Christ.

1.11.0.en: That which I have committed unto him: my faith, or my believing soul.

1.11.1.en: By Paul's trust in Christ and with the support of His grace, he endures the chains of prison and all sufferings and is not ashamed of them, because the power of Christ, in whom he believed, is boundless, and His love deserves that he give his whole life for Him.

1.11.2.en: If you meet sufferings in your life through no fault of your own, accept them for God's sake, trusting in His help, for in this you share His sufferings. Continue your service to Him and offering love to everyone, and in this you will be a true son to Him.

1.12.0.en: The Apostle Paul asks his disciple to hold fast the faith which he taught him, not only in words but also in practical conduct in love for all, so that he may be a living image of Christ in his speech and conduct.

1.13.0.en: He also asks him to hold fast the faith by the power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in him, however much the heresies around him resist him or afflictions confront him that try to make him give up his Christian life.

1.13.1.en: Do not please people by being lax in your right conduct in order to join them. As much as you are kind with them, be also careful, and flee from everything that causes you to stumble and separates you from Christ. And beware of teachings foreign to the Church, holding fast with all exactness what you received from the Fathers.

1.14.s.en: (5) The support of Paul's children for him

1.14.0.en: Asia: a region within Asia Minor, which is present-day Turkey.

1.14.1.en: Besides Paul's sufferings in prison, he endured psychological hardships because his children turned away from him, either out of fear of Nero, who had arrested him, or seeking their own comfort and benefit, the best known of them being "Phygellus and Hermogenes", who were two of his disciples and abandoned him.

1.15.0.en: On the other hand, Paul prays for his children who cared for him during his imprisonment, among them Onesiphorus, who had died by the time the epistle was written, so he asks mercy and grace from God for the members of his household, since they are without a provider, and God provides for them and cares for them.

1.16.0.en: Onesiphorus believed at the hands of Paul. He was working as a merchant in Ephesus, and in the course of his trade he came to Rome, and when he learned of Paul's imprisonment he asked where he was and took care to serve him, making light of the dangers of being arrested or harmed.

1.17.0.en: Paul prays for the soul of Onesiphorus, which is in Paradise, that it may find mercy from Christ on the day of judgment and that He may bring it into the Kingdom.

1.17.1.en: And he reminds Timothy of Onesiphorus's many services in the Church of Ephesus, which Timothy knows because he is the bishop of that city.

1.17.2.en: Be concerned for those in affliction, to show your love for them and to pray for them, for this supports them and becomes a cause of blessing for you.

2.0.0.en: As St. Paul speaks with his disciple Timothy about spiritual striving, he shows the tender feelings of his fatherhood, calling him "my son", and he offers him the help necessary for striving, which is the grace of God, for reliance in striving is not on human abilities or emotional impulse but on the grace of God.

2.1.0.en: Among many witnesses: Timothy's fellow disciples who were taught by Paul.

2.1.1.en: Commit thou: hand it over with care.

2.1.2.en: Faithful men: who have the ability and competence to teach others.

2.1.3.en: The most important matter in ministry and evangelism is making disciples of people and handing on to them the sound teachings and Christian conduct, and that they have the ability to teach others.

2.2.0.en: Paul likens his disciple Timothy and every servant in the Church to the soldier, who endures many hardships in war in order to please the king for whom he enlisted; how much more must the one who has enlisted for the service of Christ endure the hardships of ministry with contentment and joy.

2.3.0.en: Just as the soldier devotes his mind and his life to soldiering and cannot do any other work, however great or good, so Paul warns his disciple against being occupied with the affairs of life, because his only aim is to please Christ, for whom he enlisted. So he uses life with all its works and is faithful in them to meet the needs of the body, but the whole heart is occupied with the love of God and His service.

2.4.0.en: He also likens the one who strives spiritually to the competitor in athletic games, who must keep to certain training and observe a discipline in his food and sleep in order to win. Likewise the one who strives must keep to the teachings of the Church and the guidance of his father of confession and not walk according to his own personal inclination, lest the devil deceive him despite his good striving and lead him astray, whether by lessening the striving in a certain matter so that he loses his carefulness, or by excess in an exercise so that he grows weary and burdened, or by using a spiritual exercise that does not suit him.

2.5.0.en: He gives a third example of the spiritual striver, the husbandman, who performs the first operation in cultivating the land, yet he finds no fruit from it until after a long time, after all the agricultural operations are completed, ending with the harvest, and he must wait this whole time. Therefore the one who strives spiritually should be patient, for God's help and comforts may come after a long period, and sometimes he receives the reward in eternity, but all this is reckoned by God, and He allows what suits each person and builds him up spiritually. And God reassures the striver that he will surely receive his reward, for the smallest labor is very precious to God. And just as the husbandman is the one who deserves to receive his wages first, before all who labored after him in the subsequent agricultural operations, so it is with the striver, for God appreciates the extent of his labor and patience, and whoever labored more has a greater reward.

2.6.0.en: Because of the importance of the Apostle Paul's words about spiritual striving, he urges Timothy to understand the details he mentioned and reassures him that the Holy Spirit can give him understanding as long as he asks for it.

2.7.0.en: Raised: he speaks of Christ, who became like us by His Incarnation, that is, took the form of weakness, but God raised Him on the third day, that is, He rose by His divinity. All this is to encourage us, however great our weakness, that we shall be crowned after our striving and our sufferings.

2.7.1.en: Of the seed of David: that is, of the royal seed, indeed He is the King of kings. If He suffered, strove and was patient, how much more should we humans complete our striving with patience.

2.7.2.en: My gospel: my evangelism, that is, as Paul preaches, so he believes and teaches.

2.7.3.en: He presents Christ, who is the supreme example in spiritual striving, for after enduring all the sufferings He rose in great glory.

2.8.0.en: Wherein: in Christ, whom I preach.

2.8.1.en: Because Christ strove and suffered and then rose, Paul endures the labors of ministry and appears as an evildoer thrown into prison although he is innocent. Then he adds that the binding of his hands with chains does not prevent him from continuing to preach, because the word of God cannot be bound, and our tongue continues to bear witness to the truth even if they bind our body or torture us.

2.9.0.en: Paul made clear that he endures sufferings for the sake of Christ, who suffered for him, and in this verse he shows another purpose for enduring the labors of striving, which is the salvation of the souls of those to whom he preaches, who will believe because God chose them, and so they receive salvation as we also receive it, and more than this, they receive glory with us in the Kingdom of Heaven.

2.10.0.en: It is a faithful saying: to show the importance of what he is about to say.

2.10.1.en: Since Paul was bound in prison and the time of his martyrdom was near, he declares that if we suffer even to death, eternal life with Christ awaits us in heaven.

2.11.0.en: Here he affirms the reward for everyone who is patient in his striving and ministry, which is that he will reign with Christ in eternity.

2.11.1.en: On the other hand, if we deny Christ by neglecting our spiritual life or being lax in our ministry and responsibilities, divine justice is carried out in us in that He denies us in heaven and does not give us a place with Him, and consequently we are cast into eternal torment. And of course the labors we endure today cannot be measured against the glory of heaven, and on the other side, laxity and falling into pleasures and comfort today cannot be measured against eternal torment.

2.12.0.en: If we do not continue to hold fast our faith, our striving and our ministry, God will remain faithful in carrying out His word with us, that is, He confesses in heaven the one who confesses Him on earth, and denies and rejects in heaven the one who denies Him on earth.

2.12.1.en: Likewise our unfaithfulness in our ministry does not nullify the faithfulness of God, who does not deprive the souls we neglected of His love and sends to them someone to call them to Him that they may be saved, but as for us, He will reject us because of our unfaithfulness.

2.12.2.en: Your striving and your labor is a fellowship in the Cross of Christ, and His help will support you in this striving, so trust in His concern for your labor and His rewarding you with comforts on earth and glories in heaven. Seize every opportunity to labor for Him, and even prefer labor to rest, that you may enjoy His fellowship and rejoice with true joy.

2.13.0.en: These things: spiritual striving, its importance, and its reward as mentioned (vv. 1-13). Before the Lord: he speaks to people while conscious of God's presence before him, so he speaks with power and exactness.

2.13.1.en: Strive about words: to dispute in discussions that lead to heated feelings and divisions.

2.13.2.en: He asks Timothy to teach and remind the people in Ephesus of what he told him about spiritual striving, and to charge them strongly to reject the harmful philosophical discussions proclaimed by the Gnostics, who claim that this is knowledge, although they are vain discussions that disturb people and draw them away from concern for their spiritual life, so that they ruin their souls and lead them to perdition. These Gnostics proclaimed that knowledge is the basis of salvation, and they went astray in their beliefs and thought that Christ is a god created by God.

2.14.0.en: He also asks Timothy to care for the salvation of his own soul, that is, his spiritual life, so that he may be pleasing to God and accepted before Him, indeed a servant working his ministry faithfully, so that he may have boasting before God and not shame. And he concentrates on explaining the word of God in all its details for the benefit of the hearers, without any personal aim or thought of his own.

2.15.0.en: He also warns him against the useless discussions of the Gnostics, which are indeed deviations from the truth and defile a person's mind, and since they draw him away from God he is exposed to falling into many sins, indeed to counting them permissible, because they considered the body defiled and slipped into many sins.

2.16.0.en: Canker: a disease consisting of sores in the skin that corrupt it until that part of the body dies.

2.16.1.en: He likens the talk of the Gnostics to a disease that corrupts the souls of the hearers and destroys them, and he gives as an example of these Gnostics two persons, Hymenaeus and Philetus, who were two false Christian teachers, for they held Gnostic thought and claimed that the resurrection had already happened to spirits only and that therefore there is no need for the resurrection of bodies, because the body in their view is unclean, base and dust and does not deserve to rise, as we believe in the last resurrection, and by this they corrupt and lead astray the believers in the Church.

2.16.2.en: As for us, we believe in the first resurrection, that is, repentance, and the second resurrection on the day of judgment, which is the resurrection of body and spirit.

2.17.0.en: The foundation of God: faith in Christ.

2.17.2.en: Nameth the name of Christ: that is, a Christian.

2.17.3.en: The Apostle Paul reassures Timothy and all believers that the faith they received stands firm within them, as long as they are subject to the seal of the Holy Spirit which they received in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, for He guides them to reject these deviations of faith and the heresies of the Gnostics. And he also reassures them that God knows His true believing children and is patient with the Gnostic heretics who are inside the Church.

2.17.4.en: But he warns the believers against mixing with these heretical Gnostics or discussing with them, lest their minds be confused by their talk and be distracted from God.

2.18.1.en: Silver: signifies the word of God.

2.18.2.en: Wood: signifies those easily exposed to being burned by lusts and sins.

2.18.3.en: Earth: signifies those easily exposed to breaking and crushing, so they return to their earthly, bodily life, leaving their spiritual nature which they received in Baptism.

2.18.4.en: So that the people of the Church may not be troubled by some going astray after Gnostic ideas, he states a fact, which is the necessity of the presence of the wicked with the righteous within the Church, and he likens the Church to a house in which there are many vessels, some honorable and great, such as those made of gold and silver, and others base, made of wood and earth, and this too is found in the Church; some teachers and people hold fast to the faith and have a strong spiritual life, like the vessels of silver and gold, and others are exposed to perdition by burning, like wood, or to breaking and crushing so that they become like dust, like earth.

2.19.0.en: These: the ideas of the Gnostics and their vain discussions.

2.19.2.en: The Apostle concludes his words about the vain ideas of the Gnostics by encouraging the believers to reject this talk and to purge their minds and lives from it, and in this they become vessels of honor in the sight of God, who fills them with His grace, and their hearts become consecrated to Christ, and He uses them in every work of goodness and service for the benefit of the Church.

2.19.3.en: Examine yourself: do your words and discussions build up your life and those who hear you, or do they make you and them stumble?? And know that your speech is an expression of what is inside you, so cleanse yourself of bad thoughts, and express everything good within you in words for edification, and keep away from those who make you stumble.

2.20.0.en: The first quality of the children of God is their guarding against youthful lusts, whether by sight or thought or any association with the wicked who are immersed in the lusts of impurity. Every person must be careful, even if he holds a priestly rank like Timothy the bishop, or even if he is advanced in age, because Satan fights everyone. Whoever flees humbly from the sources of evil, God keeps him pure, for this fleeing is a proof of his spiritual strength.

2.20.1.en: The second quality to which St. Paul encourages is the positive side, and it includes:

2.20.2.en: Righteousness: that is, works of goodness and uprightness.

2.20.3.en: Faith: all the spiritual practices of prayers, fasts, readings and attachment to the Holy Sacraments.

2.20.4.en: Charity: good relations with the believers, forgiveness toward those who err, and that the heart be open to everyone.

2.20.5.en: Peace: seeking peace with all, even enemies and offenders, for although we keep away from associating with them and their evils, our hearts remain pure toward them and we pray for them.

2.20.6.en: Them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart: association with believers who pray to God with pure hearts, that is, repentant of sin and seeking to cling to God and to love people.

2.21.0.en: The third quality that St. Paul asks of his disciple Timothy and all the children of God is avoiding unprofitable discussions, because they produce heated feelings, quarrels and disputes among people, even inside the Church.

2.22.0.en: The fourth quality of the children of God is tenderness and encouragement toward sinners so that they may repent and we do not fall with them into quarrel or dispute, but by our calmness we remove their agitation and bring them back to truth and peace. The fifth quality for priests, of whom Timothy the bishop is the example, is that they be able to teach others the word of God that they may attain salvation.

2.22.1.en: The sixth quality is endurance and patience in the labors of spiritual striving and ministry.

2.23.0.en: The snare of the devil: sin or deviation from the faith.

2.23.1.en: Taken captive by him at his will: they came to proclaim evil, want it and hold fast to it.

2.23.2.en: The seventh quality of pastors and servants is firmness and discipline toward those who err and those who deviate from the faith, but this discipline is accompanied by meekness and calm, so that the opposers may see in them a fatherhood that brings them back to Christ and the Church, and they may leave their error and live in the divine truth. And so they are delivered from the trap of Satan into which they had fallen and return to God.

2.23.3.en: Care for the growth of your spiritual life and your love for God, and guard against the sources of sin with all exactness; in this you keep your peace and are even able to serve others and win them to Christ.
